models.name: Original Prusa MK4S
models.summary: Open-frame Cartesian workhorse equipped with Nextruder planetary direct drive, heatsink Load Cell automatic first-layer sensing, high-flow CHT nozzle, and 360° turbine part cooling.

fdmSpecs.hotendType: Prusa Nextruder with High-Flow brass CHT-style nozzle
fdmSpecs.buildPlateType: Magnetic MK52 Heatbed with Smooth, Satin, or Textured PEI Spring Steel Sheet
fdmSpecs.bedLevelingHardware: Nextruder heatsink Load Cell sensor (direct nozzle-to-sheet probing; rigid bed standoffs)

knownLimitations: Heat-soak the large 350mm aluminum bed for 10–15 minutes before running QGL and Bed Mesh when printing large parts, as thermal expansion bows the bed slightly.

questions.prompt: Which visual pattern best matches your first layer on the build plate?
questions.helpText: Inspect the very first extruded lines before the second layer prints.

options.label: Round strands dragged loose across the plate (Nozzle too high)
options.explanation: Extruded lines look round like spaghetti, do not touch adjacent lines, and peel off immediately behind the nozzle.

options.label: Translucent smears, rough ploughed ridges, or clicking (Nozzle too low)
options.explanation: Nozzle scrapes the build plate; plastic squeezes out the sides in sharp upward ridges or stops extruding altogether.

options.label: Good squish on one side, loose or scraping on the opposite corner
options.explanation: First layer thickness changes noticeably from left-to-right or front-to-back across the bed.

options.label: Sticks initially, then corners curl upward after 5–20 layers (Warping)
options.explanation: First layer goes down flat, but thermal shrinkage pulls sharp corners off the bed later in the print.

questions.prompt: How was the build plate cleaned or changed before this print?
questions.helpText: Skin oils and residual PLA sugars frequently resist 70% rubbing alcohol alone.

options.label: Touched with bare hands or wiped only with alcohol / dry cloth
options.explanation: Isopropyl alcohol dissolves light dust but often spreads skin oils thinly across textured PEI valleys.

options.label: Recently swapped between Smooth and Textured build plates
options.explanation: Different steel sheets have different coating thicknesses (~0.3–0.4 mm difference) and slicer temperature profiles.

options.label: Scrubbed with warm water and plain dish soap, dried without touching
options.explanation: Surface contamination is unlikely to be the primary cause.

questions.prompt: On your automatic-leveling printer, what was the condition of the nozzle tip before probing?
questions.helpText: Shown only for printers equipped with automatic nozzle/load-cell/strain-gauge or probe leveling.

options.label: Hardened plastic dot on nozzle tip, or pre-print leveling was skipped
options.explanation: A 0.2 mm hardened plastic dot on a nozzle-probing printer tricks the load cell/strain gauge into stopping 0.2 mm too high.

options.label: Nozzle tip wiped clean and auto-leveling ran before the print
options.explanation: Probing ran cleanly; points toward Z-offset sheet profile, loose hotend mount screws, or thermal draft warping.

questions.prompt: When did you last check the 4 manual bed tramming wheels and carriage V-wheels?
questions.helpText: Shown only when your selected printer uses verified manual screw/wheel tramming.

options.label: Have not trammed the 4 corner wheels recently, or bed wobbles slightly
options.explanation: Spring compression drift or loose Y-carriage eccentric nuts shifts nozzle clearance across the plate.

options.label: Recently trammed all 4 corners with paper/feeler gauge at bed temp
options.explanation: Mechanical corner heights are close; check bed center bow, Z-endstop switch repeatability, or surface prep.

questions.prompt: What happens to extrusion flow during the print?
questions.helpText: Distinguishing complete blockages from intermittent starvation narrows the hotend fault.

options.label: Zero plastic exits the nozzle; extruder clicks or grinds a crescent notch in filament
options.explanation: Complete blockage in the nozzle orifice, heatbreak, or tangled spool preventing feed.

options.label: Prints fine for 20–60 minutes, then gradually thins out and jams mid-print
options.explanation: Classic heat creep signature: heat rises above the melt zone and softens PLA/PETG inside the cold-end or extruder gears.

options.label: Consistent thin, spongy walls and gaps from the very start of the print
options.explanation: Partial nozzle clog, cracked extruder tension arm, wrong nozzle diameter/volumetric speed in slicer, or wet filament.

options.label: Bulging corners, rough scarred top layers, and dimensional bloat (Over-extrusion)
options.explanation: Flow ratio / extrusion multiplier or filament diameter setting pushes excess molten volume.

questions.prompt: Were you printing inside a closed enclosure or after switching from a high-temp filament?
questions.helpText: Leftover ABS/ASA/PC polymer requires higher purge temperatures than PLA.

options.label: Printing PLA/TPU with enclosure door & top glass closed (or chamber heater ON)
options.explanation: PLA glass transition (~55–60°C) is easily exceeded inside closed CoreXY chambers, flattening filament in the extruder gears.

options.label: Previously printed ABS, ASA, PETG, or Carbon-Fiber filament before loading PLA
options.explanation: Residual 260°C polymer or carbon fibers remain solid at 210°C PLA temperatures, creating an instant partial clog.

options.label: Open air / vented chamber with the same filament family
options.explanation: Points toward mechanical extruder tension, spool path friction, or nozzle debris.

questions.prompt: Which surface defect matches your print most closely?
questions.helpText: Compare travel-move hairs against perimeter seam bumps and overhang droop.

options.label: Fine spiderweb hairs or branched coral strings across empty travel spaces
options.explanation: Molten filament oozes from nozzle pressure or steam bubbles during non-print travel moves.

options.label: Random pimples, zits, or heavy vertical Z-seam scars on outer walls
options.explanation: Caused by moisture popping, power-loss recovery SD write pauses, or uncalibrated Pressure Advance / coasting.

options.label: Sagging bridges, curled overhangs, or rough pillowed top surfaces
options.explanation: Insufficient part cooling airflow, printing too hot/fast for overhang cooling, or too few top solid layers.

options.label: Pinholes or narrow unbonded gaps between perimeters and infill
options.explanation: Pressure Advance / Linear Advance K-factor set too high, or Arachne wall generator thin-wall starvation.

questions.prompt: Has the filament spool been actively dried, and do you hear faint popping at the nozzle?
questions.helpText: Even factory-sealed vacuum bags frequently arrive damp from water-bath manufacturing.

options.label: Spool stored in open room air / new un-dried PETG, TPU, or Nylon; or faint sizzling sound
options.explanation: Absorbed moisture flashes to steam at 200°C+, expanding molten plastic out of the nozzle regardless of retraction settings.

options.label: Actively dried in a filament dryer within the last 24 hours
options.explanation: Moisture is ruled out; focus on nozzle temperature, retraction distance/speed, z-hop, and part cooling.

questions.prompt: What geometric failure occurred during motion?
questions.helpText: Check whether the base stayed anchored to the bed or detached completely.

options.label: Part base is still stuck to the bed, but upper layers shifted sideways in a sharp step
options.explanation: Stepper motor lost steps, belt jumped teeth, or motor pulley grub screw slipped on the D-shaft.

options.label: Wavy echoing ripples (ringing / ghosting) repeating after sharp corners or text
options.explanation: Frame/table resonance or uncalibrated Input Shaping / belt tension mismatch.

options.label: Part knocked off the bed or printed into a tangled bird-nest in mid-air (Spaghetti)
options.explanation: Adhesion failure, missing supports on mid-air islands, or nozzle colliding with curled overhangs / grid infill.

questions.prompt: Did you hear scraping noises across infill or curling overhangs right before the failure?
questions.helpText: Crossing infill patterns like Grid accumulate double-height intersections at high speeds.

options.label: Yes — audible nozzle rumbling across Grid/Triangles infill or curled overhang corners
options.explanation: High-speed toolhead impact against raised plastic skips belt steps or knocks tall parts off the plate.

options.label: No scraping — happened on simple geometry or at the same axis travel direction
options.explanation: Strongly points to loose belt tension, loose stepper pulley set screw, cable snag, or resonance.

questions.prompt: Which subsystem reported an error or failed to complete its sequence?
questions.helpText: Select whether the fault happens during bed probing or filament loading/swapping.

options.label: Bed mesh probing or Z-homing aborts with a sensor / loadcell / strain-gauge error
options.explanation: Probe signal anomaly, debris under bed frame, overtightened heatsink screws, or disconnected sensor cable.

options.label: Single-spool filament will not load past the sensor or extruder entrance
options.explanation: Bent filament tip catching PTFE chamfer, stuck filament sensor lever/magnet, or broken brittle PLA segment inside path.

options.label: Multi-color unit (AMS / MMU / CFS / ACE / IFS) fails to retract, feed, or clear purge chute
options.explanation: Cardboard spool rim slip, sharp PTFE bend friction, worn filament cutter blade, or backed-up purge chute.

questions.prompt: Where did the resin print separate during the job?
questions.helpText: Inspect BOTH the aluminum build plate and the bottom of the resin vat (use plastic scraper gently—never metal!).

options.label: Build plate is completely empty; cured flat silhouette stuck to vat release film
options.explanation: First bottom layers never bonded to the metal build plate due to Z-zero gap, cold resin, or insufficient bottom exposure.

options.label: Raft and supports printed on the plate, but the model ripped off the support tips
options.explanation: Cross-sectional peel force exceeded support tip strength due to normal exposure too low, unvented hollow suction cup, or light supports.

options.label: Model printed partially, but horizontal layers split apart or shifted mid-print
options.explanation: Inter-layer delamination caused by cold resin (<20°C), insufficient rest/wait-before-print time, stretched FEP film, or adding cold resin mid-print.

questions.prompt: What is the resin temperature and model geometry?
questions.helpText: Photopolymer viscosity doubles below 18°C, dramatically increasing peel suction forces.

options.label: Unheated room/garage below 21°C (70°F) without vat pre-heating
options.explanation: Cold viscous resin cannot flow out from beneath the build plate quickly, preventing bottom cure and causing layer splits.

options.label: Large flat cross-section parallel to screen, or hollowed model without drain holes near the base
options.explanation: Creates vacuum suction against the FEP/PFA film on every peel cycle, ripping models off supports.

options.label: Warm resin (25–30°C) and model angled 30–45° with drain holes
options.explanation: Points toward normal/bottom exposure calibration, worn release film tension, or smooth build plate surface.

questions.prompt: What abnormal curing pattern appears on the cured resin part?
questions.helpText: Remove the resin vat and place a plain sheet of white paper over the glass before running a screen test—never look directly into bare UV LEDs.

options.label: Clean vertical cylindrical tunnels/holes piercing straight through the print
options.explanation: Dead LCD pixel clusters or cured resin spots stuck on the screen protector blocking UV light.

options.label: Entire screen rectangle or thick verticalpillars cure into solid blocks
options.explanation: Loose/damaged LCD ribbon cable failing to mask UV light, corrupted USB slice file, or failing mono LCD panel.

options.label: Soft/muddy fine details, fused tolerances, or swollen support side-surfaces
options.explanation: Normal layer exposure time too high for your resin opacity, or high-scatter ACF film paired with excessive UV power.

causes.title: Build Plate Skin Oil or Sugar Residue Contamination
causes.plainExplanation: Fingerprints, skin oils, and degraded PLA/PETG release residues coat the microscopic pores of PEI sheets. Wiping with 70% isopropyl alcohol often spreads oils into a thin film rather than lifting them off, causing extruded strands to skate and curl immediately.
distinguishingChecks: Water droplet test: Rinse plate under tap water—if water beads up unevenly in patches, oil film is present.
Check whether adhesion fails worst near the front edge or center where hands grip flexed parts.
causes.safetyNotes: Allow the heated bed to cool below 40°C before removing the magnetic spring steel plate.

causes.title: Nozzle-Contact Probing Skewed by Tip Residue or Sheet Offset
causes.plainExplanation: Your printer uses automated nozzle-contact, load-cell, or strain-gauge probing rather than manual bed wheels. If a tiny hardened dot of plastic sits on the nozzle tip during probing—or if you swapped between Smooth and Textured build plates without re-probing—the sensor registers contact prematurely and prints the first layer 0.1–0.3 mm too high in mid-air.
distinguishingChecks: Inspect the brass/hardened nozzle tip and rear silicone wiper pad for stuck filament.
Verify "Auto Bed Leveling" was enabled at print start after changing build plates.
On Bambu A1/A1 mini, check that the hotend latch clip is fully locked and rear heater screws are snug.
causes.safetyNotes: Nozzle reaches 150–250°C during cleaning. Use brass wire brush (avoid thermistor wires) or silicone wiper—never fingers.

causes.title: Non-Contact Probe Z-Offset / Steel Sheet Profile Mismatch
causes.plainExplanation: Printers with inductive/capacitive proximity probes (such as Prusa MK3S+ SuperPINDA or Elegoo Neptune 4 inductive sensor) map bed tilt automatically, but measure distance to the metal core—NOT the nozzle tip. Swapping from a Smooth PEI sheet to a thinner Textured PEI sheet without updating Live-Z or Steel Sheet profiles leaves the nozzle ~0.30 mm too high.
distinguishingChecks: Confirm which build sheet profile is active on the LCD (e.g., Smooth1 vs Textur1 on MK3S+, or saved Z-offset in Neptune 4 Level menu).
Observe a 1-layer calibration square: separate round lines mean Z-offset needs to be more negative (closer to plate).
causes.safetyNotes: Lower Live-Z in small 0.025 mm increments while watching extrusion so the nozzle never gouges the PEI coating.

causes.title: Out-of-Tram Manual Bed Adjustment Wheels or Loose Eccentric Nuts
causes.plainExplanation: Your printer relies on spring-loaded manual corner hand-wheels (or hybrid auxiliary tramming wheels) to align the heated bed plane parallel to the X/Y gantry. Vibration and thermal cycles relax spring tension, causing uneven squish across corners.
distinguishingChecks: With printer cool, gently try to rock the build plate corners—if the Y-carriage wobbles, snug the hexagonal eccentric nuts under the bed BEFORE touching corner leveling wheels.
Preheat bed to 60°C and compare 0.10 mm feeler gauge friction directly above all 4 bed screws.
causes.safetyNotes: Heat only the bed (60°C) and keep the nozzle cool or wiped clean so you do not burn fingers while sliding a feeler gauge.

causes.title: Thermal Shrinkage Warping & Cooling Drafts
causes.plainExplanation: Upper layers cool and contract, pulling upward on bottom corners. Cold room drafts, AC vents, excessive part-cooling fan speed on layers 1–3, or printing ABS/ASA/PC without a warm draft-free enclosure causes corners to peel off even clean build plates.
distinguishingChecks: Check slicer Cooling tab: verify part-cooling fan is 0% for the first 1–3 layers (3–5 layers for PETG/ABS).
For sharp rectangular footprints >100 mm, check whether adding a 5–8 mm Outer Brim with 0.1 mm brim-object gap anchors corners.
causes.safetyNotes: When printing ABS or ASA in an enclosure, use activated carbon/HEPA filtration or ventilate styrene fumes away from living spaces.

causes.title: Partial or Complete Nozzle Orifice Blockage (Cold Pull Needed)
causes.plainExplanation: Carbonized polymer, metallic/carbon-fiber filler particles, or leftover higher-temperature filament (such as ABS/PETG left in the melt zone when printing PLA at 210°C) restricts the 0.4 mm nozzle orifice, starving extrusion and making extruder gears skip.
distinguishingChecks: Raise Z by 100 mm, heat nozzle to 250°C, and command 50 mm manual extrude in air: if filament curls sharply sideways instead of falling straight down, a partial wall clog is present.
If printing CF/GF/Glow filament with a 0.2 mm or 0.4 mm nozzle, verify fiber bridging has not jammed the taper.
causes.safetyNotes: Hotend reaches 250–270°C. Wear heat-resistant gloves when gripping filament or brass nozzles; never clear clogs with power on near exposed heater wires.

causes.title: Heat Creep / Enclosed Chamber Filament Softening in Extruder
causes.plainExplanation: When chamber ambient temperature exceeds ~40–45°C (common when printing PLA inside closed CoreXY printers like Bambu P1S/X1C, Creality K1C, Elegoo Centauri, or QIDI Plus4) or when the hotend heatsink fan is dusty/failing, PLA softens prematurely inside the extruder drive gears, flattens out, and jams 20–60 minutes into a print.
distinguishingChecks: Pull out the jammed filament tip: if it shows a thickened bulbous plug or flattened gear teeth marks above the melt zone, heat creep occurred.
Confirm hotend heatsink cooling fan spins immediately whenever nozzle temp exceeds 50°C.
causes.safetyNotes: Power off and cool hotend before disassembling direct-drive extruder front covers or filament cutters.

causes.title: Moisture-Absorbed Filament Flashing to Steam in Nozzle
causes.plainExplanation: PETG, TPU, Nylon (PA), PC, PVA, and older PLA absorb atmospheric humidity. Inside a 215–260°C hotend, trapped water boils into micro-steam bubbles that push molten plastic out during travel moves—creating cobweb stringing, pitted zits, and brittle layer bonding that slicer retraction tuning cannot cure.
distinguishingChecks: Listen closely near the nozzle during extrusion for faint hissing/popping sounds and watch for steam puffs or matte rough extrusion.
Dry the spool in an active convection filament dryer (e.g., 50°C for PLA, 65°C for PETG, 75–80°C for PA/PC) for 6–8 hours and reprint the exact same G-code.
causes.safetyNotes: Never exceed the spool hub softening temperature or use uncalibrated kitchen gas ovens to dry filament.

causes.title: Excessive Nozzle Temp, Z-Hop Ooze, or Pressure Advance Mismatch
causes.plainExplanation: Even with dry filament, printing 10–15°C hotter than needed lowers melt viscosity, while excessive spiral/normal Z-hop or wrong retraction distance (e.g. >1.5 mm on an all-metal direct drive) pulls air or leaves fine wisps. Pinholes at seam starts or wall gaps indicate Pressure Advance (K-value) is set too high.
distinguishingChecks: Verify retraction distance matches your extruder type: 0.4–1.0 mm for Direct Drive vs 3.5–5.5 mm for Bowden.
Run a 5°C step temperature tower and OrcaSlicer/Bambu Studio Pressure Advance line/pattern calibration.

causes.title: X/Y Belt Tension Slip, Loose Stepper Grub Screw, or Grid Infill Collision
causes.plainExplanation: Layer shifts happen when the toolhead’s commanded position decouples from physical carriage position. Common triggers include nozzle collisions with crossing infill patterns (like Grid), loose X/Y timing belts, or a stepper motor pulley grub screw (set screw) slipping on the flat of the motor shaft.
distinguishingChecks: Switch slicer infill pattern from Grid/Triangles to Gyroid or Cross Hatch (non-crossing within the same layer) and enable "Avoid crossing walls".
Draw a sharpie witness mark across the stepper motor shaft tip and toothed pulley hub—run a fast print and check if the line splits.
causes.safetyNotes: Power off printer before inspecting belts or tightening motor pulley grub screws so pinch points cannot move unexpectedly.

causes.title: Multi-Material PTFE Path Friction, Cardboard Spool Slip, or Cutter Wear
causes.plainExplanation: Automated filament changers (Bambu AMS, Prusa MMU3, Creality CFS, Anycubic ACE Pro, Flashforge IFS) push and pull filament meters through PTFE tubes and buffers. Dented cardboard spool rims slip on rollers, tight PTFE bends bind filament, and dull toolhead cutter blades leave deformed tails that jam on retraction.
distinguishingChecks: Inspect PTFE tube entry into the toolhead—ensure minimum 60–80 mm gentle bend radius without kinks against top glass.
Snap plastic rim adapters onto cardboard spools (and never use dusty torn rims inside roller-driven AMS/CFS bays).
Inspect toolhead filament cutter blade and purge chute flapper for stuck purge coils.
causes.safetyNotes: Keep fingers clear of spring-loaded filament cutter levers and motorized buffer gears.

causes.title: Cold Resin Viscosity, Vacuum Suction Cup, or Under-Exposed Bottom/Normal Layers
causes.plainExplanation: MSLA resin curing is an exothermic chemical reaction that slows drastically below 22°C. Cold thick resin cannot squeeze out fully before UV turn-on (causing bottom detachment or pancake rafts), while unvented hollow cavities or under-exposed support tips tear parts off mid-print.
distinguishingChecks: Verify resin vat temperature is 25–30°C prior to starting the print.
Check slicer preview with UVtools or island detector for unvented suction cups facing the build plate; add ≥2.5 mm drain holes right above the lowest internal cavity.
Run a tank-clean sheet removal (plastic card corner—never metal!) after ANY failed print before homing Z again, or cured debris will shatter the monochrome LCD.
causes.safetyNotes: MANDATORY PPE: Always wear nitrile gloves (never latex) and eye protection when handling liquid photopolymer resin or IPA wash baths. Ventilate workspace.

causes.title: Cured Resin on Screen Protector, Dead LCD Pixels, or Ribbon Cable Fault
causes.plainExplanation: Monochrome MSLA LCDs act as selective UV shutters. Cured resin droplets on the tempered glass protector cast permanent vertical holes through models, while a loose MIPI ribbon cable or cracked LCD polarizer allows unmasked UV blocks to cure solid bricks in the vat.
distinguishingChecks: Remove the resin vat, lay a white sheet of copy paper over the screen, and run Tools -> Screen Exposure / Logo Test.
Dark black spots inside bright areas indicate dead pixels or cured resin spots on the screen protector; glowing blocks in dark zones indicate LCD shutter/ribbon failure.
causes.safetyNotes: Never stare directly at an uncovered 405nm COB UV array during Exposure Tests—always diffuse with white paper or wear UV400 safety glasses.

guides.title: Auto-Leveling Nozzle Prep, Sensor Check & Z-Offset Calibration
toolsNeeded: Lint-free microfiber towel
Brass or silicone nozzle brush (safe for nozzle material)
Hex key (only for checking hotend mount tightness)
partsNeeded: Silicone nozzle wiper pad (inspect for wear)
safetyWarnings: Hotend heats between 140°C and 250°C during nozzle wipe and probing. Never touch the nozzle or heater block with bare skin.
Never use a conductive steel wire brush near energized heater or thermistor wires while power is ON—shorting 24V heater leads into 3.3V thermistor pins instantly destroys the toolhead board.
guides.serviceBoundaryNote: User-serviceable calibration. If load-cell or strain-gauge wiring harnesses under the heatbed are frayed or thermally damaged, stop and contact manufacturer support.

modelSpecificMenuNotes.mdl_flashforge_ad5m: Touchscreen -> Settings (Gear) -> Auto-Leveling Check -> Start. Ensure both red side nozzle clips are clicked 100% flush before probing.
modelSpecificMenuNotes.mdl_bambu_a1: Touchscreen -> Settings -> Calibration -> Auto-Bed Leveling. If Z height fluctuates randomly, remove silicone sock when cool and verify the 3 front + 4 rear heater assembly screws are tight.
modelSpecificMenuNotes.mdl_bambu_p1s: Screen -> Settings -> Calibration -> Auto Bed Leveling, and confirm the correct plate type (Textured PEI Plate vs Cool Plate) is selected in Bambu Studio.
modelSpecificMenuNotes.mdl_prusa_mk4s: LCD -> Control -> Calibration & Tests -> Loadcell Test. Gently tap nozzle only when prompted on screen; do not adjust non-existent Live-Z.
modelSpecificMenuNotes.mdl_prusa_mk3s_plus: SuperPINDA measures metal sheet, NOT nozzle tip! Go to LCD -> Settings -> HW Setup -> Steel Sheets, select a dedicated profile for Smooth vs Textured, and run Calibration -> First Layer Calibration.
modelSpecificMenuNotes.mdl_creality_k1c: Touchscreen -> Settings -> Self-Check -> Auto Leveling. Verify rear silicone wiper strip on the build plate is intact.
modelSpecificMenuNotes.mdl_creality_ender3_v3_se: Knob Screen -> Leveling. After auto-probing finishes, run a 1-layer square and adjust Prepare -> Z-Offset by ±0.05 mm only if needed.

steps.title: Inspect Hotend Seating & Silicone Wiper
steps.instruction: With the hotend cool, gently wiggle the nozzle tip with two fingers. There must be zero vertical or rotational play in the quick-swap clip or heater block screws. Check that no stray filament poop is trapped under the magnetic build plate.
steps.expectedObservation: Build plate sits completely flat against magnetic sheet with zero trapped plastic crumbs; nozzle is rigid.
steps.commonMistake: Overlooking a tiny 0.3 mm speck of purged filament stuck underneath the magnetic PEI spring steel sheet, which creates a localized high bump.

steps.title: Heat & Clean the Nozzle Tip Before Probing
steps.instruction: Preheat the nozzle to your filament’s softening temperature (180°C for PLA, 220°C for PETG/ABS), retract filament 2 mm, and wipe the tip clean with a folded paper towel or silicone brush so bare metal contacts the plate during probing.
steps.expectedObservation: Nozzle tip cone and flat orifice rim are clean with zero hardened plastic stalactites.
steps.commonMistake: Leaving a cold hardened dot of PETG on the nozzle tip—on load-cell and strain-gauge printers, this pushes the sensor early and shifts the entire first layer too high.

steps.title: Verify Slicer Build Plate Type & Run Manufacturer Calibration
steps.instruction: Confirm your slicer Build Plate / Bed Type matches the physical plate installed (Textured PEI vs Smooth PEI changes Z-offset compensation automatically in Bambu Studio / OrcaSlicer). Run your printer’s built-in Auto-Leveling routine on a stable desk.
steps.expectedObservation: Printer completes multi-point mesh probing without table vibration or sensor timeout warnings.
steps.commonMistake: Bumping or leaning on the workbench while sensitive strain-gauge or load-cell probing is zeroing.

steps.title: Print a Single-Layer 60 × 60 mm Verification Patch
steps.instruction: Slice and print a 0.20 mm high single-layer square. Peel it off once cool and flex it along the extrusion lines.
steps.expectedObservation: Adjacent extrusion lines fuse into a single flexible sheet with smooth top ridges and uniform matte/textured underside.
steps.commonMistake: Turning bed screws on automatic rigid-bed printers instead of using the firmware Z-offset trim or cleaning the nozzle.

guides.verificationProcedure: Peel the 60 × 60 mm 0.20 mm test square from the cooled plate and bend it 90° across the layer lines—lines must stay fused without splitting like window blinds (too high) or feeling razor-thin and rough (too low).

ifNotFixedBranches.label: Lines look squished properly, but still peel off the plate
Extrusion lines have porous gaps even at proper height

guides.title: Manual 4-Corner Bed Tramming & Eccentric Nut Alignment
symptoms: Nozzle too high on one corner and scraping on another
toolsNeeded: 0.10 mm metal feeler gauge (preferred) or standard 80gsm A4 copy paper
10 mm flat wrench (for eccentric nuts if carriage wobbles)
partsNeeded: Silicone bed mounts or stiff yellow die springs (optional upgrade if stock springs drift rapidly)
safetyWarnings: Heat the bed to 60°C for realistic thermal expansion, but keep the nozzle cool (or retracted & wiped clean) to avoid finger burns while moving the feeler gauge.
Never push down on the heated bed with your hand while testing gauge drag—hand pressure compresses the springs and ruins the measurement.
guides.serviceBoundaryNote: Applicable ONLY to printers equipped with user-adjustable spring-loaded corner tramming wheels (or hybrid auxiliary leveling knobs). Do not perform on load-cell rigid-bed machines.

modelSpecificMenuNotes.mdl_creality_ender3_v2: LCD -> Prepare -> Auto Home. Use LCD Move Axis (never push Z by hand) or tramming G-code macro to visit each screw position.
modelSpecificMenuNotes.mdl_elegoo_neptune_4_pro: Touchscreen -> Level -> Auxiliary Leveling (points 1–4 with wheels), THEN immediately run Auto Leveling (121-point mesh), verify center Z-offset, and tap the top-right Save icon.

steps.title: Eliminate Y-Carriage & X-Gantry V-Wheel Wobble First
steps.instruction: With printer cool, grasp opposite edges of the build plate and try to rock it gently. If it tilts or clunks, rotate the hexagonal eccentric nut(s) on the V-roller wheels underneath in tiny 15° turns just until play disappears while the bed still glides smoothly.
steps.expectedObservation: Zero rocking play in bed carriage and toolhead carriage.
steps.commonMistake: Attempting to level corner springs while the Y-carriage wheels are loose—every print move tilts the bed anew.

steps.title: Pre-Compress Corner Springs & Home Z
steps.instruction: Tighten all 4 corner wheels ~60% down so the springs have firm preload, verify the Z-endstop switch triggers cleanly before the nozzle touches glass/PEI, preheat bed to 60°C for 5 minutes, and run Auto Home.
steps.expectedObservation: Springs have firm resistance and will not vibrate loose mid-print.
steps.commonMistake: Leaving springs nearly fully decompressed, causing hand wheels to spin free from Y-axis acceleration.

steps.title: Tram All 4 Screw Positions Twice in Cross/Perimeter Passes
steps.instruction: Move the clean nozzle directly above Corner 1. Slide a 0.10 mm feeler gauge between nozzle and plate and turn the hand wheel until you feel consistent light scratchy drag. Repeat for Corners 2, 3, and 4, then repeat the entire 4-corner loop a second time (adjusting one corner pivots the opposite corner).
steps.expectedObservation: All 4 corners exhibit identical light feeler-gauge drag on the second pass without further wheel rotation.
steps.commonMistake: Doing only a single 4-corner pass—because 4 points over-constrain a plane, adjusting Corner 3 shifts Corner 1.

steps.title: Save Hybrid Mesh (If Equipped) & Run 5-Square Test Print
steps.instruction: On hybrid printers (e.g., Neptune 4 Pro or CR-Touch upgraded Ender-3), run the automatic mesh scan AFTER manual wheel tramming and save to EEPROM/printer.cfg. Print a 5-point corner + center first-layer test.
steps.expectedObservation: All 4 corner squares and center square bond evenly with fused extrusion lines.
steps.commonMistake: Forgetting to press Save / Store Settings after auxiliary + mesh calibration.

guides.verificationProcedure: Print 5 single-layer 25 × 25 mm squares (4 corners + center) and confirm uniform squish across all five patches.

ifNotFixedBranches.label: 4 corners match, but center square is higher or lower (bowed bed)
Plastic curls off despite proper gap

guides.title: Deep-Cleaning PEI / Glass Build Plates & Release Agent Rules
toolsNeeded: Unscented plain dish soap (e.g., Dawn / Fairy — no moisturizers or lanolin)
Dedicated clean nylon dish brush or non-scratch sponge
Lint-free paper towels
partsNeeded: PVA glue stick or liquid release agent (ONLY when printing PETG/PC/TPU on Smooth PEI or glass)
safetyWarnings: Never use acetone on Textured Powder-Coated PEI, Bambu Cool/Textured plates, or PC build sheets—acetone chemically crazes and destroys powder-coated PEI.
guides.serviceBoundaryNote: Routine user maintenance before prints or whenever adhesion drops.

steps.title: Scrub Plate at the Sink with Warm Water & Plain Dish Soap
steps.instruction: Remove the cooled magnetic spring steel plate from the printer. Scrub both sides under warm running water using 2 drops of plain degreasing dish soap and a clean nylon brush for 45 seconds to lift skin lipids out of textured PEI valleys.
steps.expectedObservation: Rinse water sheets smoothly across the entire plate without beading into dry oily islands.
steps.commonMistake: Using bathroom hand soap (contains moisturizing oils/aloe) or kitchen sponges previously used on greasy cookware.

steps.title: Dry Immediately by Edges Only
steps.instruction: Dry thoroughly with fresh paper towels while holding the plate strictly by its outer metal tabs. Reinstall on the magnetic heatbed without touching the print zone.
steps.expectedObservation: Matte, grease-free surface with zero lint.
steps.commonMistake: Resting thumbs on the front center of the plate while snapping it onto the magnet.

steps.title: Apply Release Barrier ONLY Where Material Chemistry Demands It
steps.instruction: For PLA on clean Textured or Smooth PEI: print directly with NO glue. For PETG, TPU, or PC on Smooth PEI or bare Glass: apply a thin, even layer of PVA glue stick as a release barrier so chemical bonding does not rip chunks out of the smooth surface.
steps.expectedObservation: PLA grips clean PEI firmly while hot and self-releases with a pop once cooled below 35°C.
steps.commonMistake: Printing PETG hot directly onto pristine Smooth PEI without a barrier, permanently welding PETG to the film.

guides.verificationProcedure: Run a brimless small calibration cube or first-layer test; verify edges remain flat through completion and release cleanly once plate cools.

ifNotFixedBranches.label: Plate is spotless, but lines still look round and un-squished

guides.title: Hotend Cold Pull, Heat-Creep Prevention & Nozzle Unclogging
toolsNeeded: 1.5 mm hex key or cold-pull PLA/Nylon cleaning filament
0.35 mm acupuncture cleaning needle (for 0.4 mm nozzle)
Heat-resistant gloves & flush cutters
partsNeeded: Replacement 0.4 mm / 0.6 mm nozzle (if internal bore is abraded)
safetyWarnings: BURN HAZARD: Hotend reaches 250–270°C during clog clearing. Wear heat-resistant gloves and keep hands below the nozzle.
ELECTRICAL HAZARD: Never insert metal hex keys or needles near exposed heater cartridge or thermistor wires while heaters are powered.
guides.serviceBoundaryNote: User-serviceable hotend maintenance. If molten plastic has encapsulated the entire heater block and wiring harness ("blob of death") around fragile thermistor leads, warm gently only if safe or replace the complete hotend assembly rather than prying cold plastic off thin wires.

modelSpecificMenuNotes.mdl_bambu_p1s: Use Bambu Wiki "Hex Key Cold Pull" or Extruder Clog removal: open top glass/front door when printing PLA so chamber stays <38°C.
modelSpecificMenuNotes.mdl_prusa_mk4s: Open Nextruder idler swivel lever on the side to inspect drive gear teeth directly before performing LCD -> Control -> Cold Pull (automated firmware cold-pull wizard!).
modelSpecificMenuNotes.mdl_creality_k1c: Flip open the silver extruder tension switch at top of toolhead to unlock gears before pulling upward on filament.
modelSpecificMenuNotes.mdl_qidi_plus4: Ensure Chamber Temperature in slicer filament settings is set to 0°C for PLA/PETG/TPU.

steps.title: Check Chamber Ventilation & Heatsink Fan First
steps.instruction: Heat nozzle to 60°C and visually confirm the hotend heatsink cooling fan (not the part-cooling blower) spins up at full RPM without dust buildup. If printing PLA on an enclosed printer, prop open the top lid or front door.
steps.expectedObservation: Hotend cooling fan runs steadily above 50°C with unobstructed heatsink fins.
steps.commonMistake: Clearing a clog without fixing a stalled heatsink fan or closed warm chamber, causing an identical heat-creep jam 30 minutes into the next print.

steps.title: Heat Above Previous Highest Material Temperature & Push Purge
steps.instruction: Raise Z-axis by 100 mm. Heat nozzle to 250–260°C (higher if PC/PA was previously loaded). Unlock extruder tensioner or command slow extrusion while pushing light PLA or cleaning Nylon downward until molten plastic flows.
steps.expectedObservation: Dark flecks or higher-temp polymer remnants purge out of the nozzle.
steps.commonMistake: Attempting to purge an ABS/PETG clog at 210°C PLA temperature, where the blockage remains solid.

steps.title: Perform a Controlled Cold Pull
steps.instruction: Keep light-colored PLA or Nylon pressed firmly into the hotend while cooling the nozzle down to 90°C (for PLA) or 115°C (for Nylon). Disengage the extruder idler gears and pull the filament straight upward smoothly and firmly.
steps.expectedObservation: Extracted filament tip shows a crisp conical mold of the internal nozzle tip along with embedded dark debris/carbon specks.
steps.commonMistake: Pulling above 140°C (filament stretches into a thin thread instead of pulling debris) or below 65°C (filament snaps inside throat).

steps.title: Inspect Extruder Gear Teeth & Free-Air Extrusion Stream
steps.instruction: Brush any ground plastic dust out of the extruder drive gear teeth, re-engage idler tension, heat to normal print temp, and extrude 50 mm in mid-air.
steps.expectedObservation: Smooth, uniform cylindrical strand drops straight down to the bed without curling sharply sideways or clicking.
steps.commonMistake: Leaving powdered filament shavings packed inside the extruder gear grooves, causing immediate grip loss.

guides.verificationProcedure: Extrude 60 mm in mid-air at normal printing temperature and confirm silent extruder rotation and a straight, uniform strand.

ifNotFixedBranches.label: Extruder still clicks or slips despite clean nozzle
Prints extrude steadily now, but show cobweb stringing

guides.title: Eliminating Stringing & Blobs: Active Drying, Temp & Retraction
guides.estimatedTime: 15 min tuning (+ 6h active spool drying if damp)
toolsNeeded: Active convection filament dryer or heated dehydrator
partsNeeded: PTFE drybox desiccant packs (storage maintenance only—desiccant alone cannot dry already-wet spools quickly)
safetyWarnings: Do not exceed spool plastic softening temperatures (keep standard ABS/PS spools ≤70°C; use high-temp spools for 80°C Nylon drying).
guides.serviceBoundaryNote: User-configurable material prep and slicer profile calibration.

steps.title: Dry the Spool Before Changing Slicer Retraction Numbers
steps.instruction: Place damp spools in a vented active filament dryer: PLA at 50°C for 5h, PETG/TPU at 60–65°C for 6–8h, ABS/ASA at 70°C for 6h, Nylon/PC at 75–80°C for 8–12h.
steps.expectedObservation: Popping/sizzling sounds at the nozzle vanish and extruded lines turn smooth and glossy.
steps.commonMistake: Chasing 4+ mm retraction distances on a direct-drive all-metal hotend to mask wet PETG—excess retraction pulls molten plastic into the cold heatbreak and causes a jam!

steps.title: Verify Direct-Drive vs Bowden Retraction Bounds
steps.instruction: Set baseline retraction according to your printer’s extruder architecture: Direct Drive all-metal = 0.4–0.8 mm @ 30–45 mm/s; Bowden tube = 3.5–5.5 mm @ 40–50 mm/s. Enable "Wipe while retracting" or Spiral Z-Hop (0.2–0.4 mm slope) if supported.
steps.expectedObservation: Clean travel break-off without dragging molten tails upward.
steps.commonMistake: Using a generic Bowden Cura profile (5 mm retraction) on a modern Direct-Drive CoreXY printer.

steps.title: Check Nozzle Temperature & Power-Loss Recovery Blobs
steps.instruction: Lower nozzle print temperature by 5–10°C within the filament’s rated range if wisps persist. On smooth curved vases/cylinders showing random surface pimples on SD-card Marlin printers, disable Power-Loss Recovery (`M413 S0`) so SD write pauses do not stall the nozzle.
steps.expectedObservation: Crisp travel towers free of branched coral strings and random outer-wall zits.
steps.commonMistake: Lowering nozzle temperature so far that inter-layer strength fails.

guides.verificationProcedure: Print a two-post 25 mm retraction test tower; zero heavy branches should bridge the gap (any microscopic whisp should brush off cleanly by hand).

ifNotFixedBranches.label: Nozzle oozes around heater block threads above tip (hotend leak)

guides.title: Resolving Layer Shifting & Ringing: Belts, Pulleys & Infill
toolsNeeded: 1.5 mm & 2.0 mm hex keys
Fine-tip permanent marker (for pulley shaft witness mark)
partsNeeded: Medium-strength blue threadlocker (Loctite 243 or equivalent) for metal stepper grub screws (keep threadlocker strictly away from polycarbonate/ABS plastic!)
safetyWarnings: PINCH HAZARD: Power off the printer before plucking belts or turning stepper pulleys.
CHEMICAL WARNING: Never let anaerobic threadlocker touch ABS or polycarbonate printed/molded toolhead parts—it causes rapid chemical stress cracking.
guides.serviceBoundaryNote: User-serviceable mechanical check. Re-run Input Shaping / Vibration Compensation after any belt tension adjustment.

modelSpecificMenuNotes.mdl_bambu_p1s: Loosen the two rear belt tensioner retention screws on back of frame, slide toolhead slowly across X/Y 3 times so spring self-tensioners equalize, re-tighten, then run Calibration -> Vibration Compensation.
modelSpecificMenuNotes.mdl_creality_k1c: Check X/Y belt tension screws and switch slicer infill from Grid to Gyroid.
modelSpecificMenuNotes.mdl_prusa_mk4s: Use the official Prusa Belt Tuner acoustic app to pluck X and Y belts to exact target Hz frequencies.

steps.title: Eliminate Slicer Nozzle-Collision Triggers
steps.instruction: In your slicer, change Infill Pattern from Grid or Triangles (which cross over already-printed lines on the same layer) to Gyroid, Cross Hatch, or Rectilinear. Enable "Reduce infill retraction" OFF so travel moves retract properly.
steps.expectedObservation: Audible nozzle scraping across solid/infill intersections disappears immediately.
steps.commonMistake: Tightening belts tighter and tighter when the true cause was high-speed nozzle impact against raised Grid infill intersections.

steps.title: Check Stepper Motor Pulley Grub Screws (Set Screws)
steps.instruction: Inspect the toothed drive pulleys on the X and Y stepper shafts. Ensure one grub screw is tightened squarely against the flat ("D-cut") of the steel motor shaft, then snug the second screw. Draw a radial marker line across shaft end and pulley hub.
steps.expectedObservation: Zero backlash when rocking the carriage slightly while holding the motor shaft stationary.
steps.commonMistake: Tightening both grub screws onto the round part of the motor shaft, allowing 1–2 mm back-and-forth slip on direction reversals.

steps.title: Equalize X/Y Belt Tension & Re-Run Input Shaping
steps.instruction: Inspect belts for missing teeth or rubbing against pulley flanges. Set equal tension per your manufacturer procedure (self-tensioner springs on Bambu CoreXY, or equal Hz belt tuner on Prusa/Voron/Cartesian), then run Input Shaping / Resonance Calibration.
steps.expectedObservation: Crisp corner transitions without echoing ghost ripples or skipped steps.
steps.commonMistake: Over-tightening belts like guitar strings, which bends stepper shafts and causes premature bearing failure.

guides.verificationProcedure: Print a 30 mm XYZ calibration cube at normal speed and measure X/Y walls with digital calipers—walls must be vertical with zero staircase steps.

ifNotFixedBranches.label: Print detaches completely from bed rather than shifting layers

guides.title: Multi-Color Filament Changer Recovery (AMS / CFS / MMU / ACE)
toolsNeeded: Flush diagonal cutters (cut clean 45° or straight filament tip per manual)
partsNeeded: PTFE tubing (2.5 mm ID × 4.0 mm OD recommended for low multi-material friction)
safetyWarnings: Do not forcefully yank filament backward through closed extruder gears—release extruder tension or heat & cut first.

modelSpecificMenuNotes.mdl_bambu_p1s: HMS 0700 family: Check PTFE bend right above toolhead glass lid; add a PTFE guide clip or riser if top glass pinches the tube.
modelSpecificMenuNotes.mdl_creality_k2_plus: Verify CFS hub buffer moves freely and cardboard spools have undamaged round edges.

steps.title: Check Spool Rim Condition & Brittle Filament Breaks
steps.instruction: Inspect the active spool for tangled cross-under loops or dented cardboard rims. Bend the tip of PLA filament 90°—if it snaps like dry pasta, dry it before feeding through multi-tube hubs so segments do not shatter inside internal manifolds.
steps.expectedObservation: Spool rolls smoothly on rollers without wobbling or binding.
steps.commonMistake: Placing electrical tape loosely on cardboard rims where adhesive gums up rubber drive rollers.

steps.title: Inspect PTFE Tube Entry Radius & Worn Grooves
steps.instruction: Disconnect the quick-coupler at the toolhead/buffer and check the PTFE tube interior for worn grooves or sharp kinks against the enclosure top glass.
steps.expectedObservation: Filament slides effortlessly by hand from spool bay to toolhead with minimal drag.
steps.commonMistake: Replacing 2.5 mm ID multi-material PTFE tubing with tight 1.9 mm ID Capricorn Bowden tubing, which causes severe retraction friction in AMS/MMU paths!

steps.title: Inspect Filament Cutter Blade & Purge Chute
steps.instruction: Verify the toolhead filament cutter lever snaps back smoothly and the blade edge is unchipped. Clear any coiled purge waste stuck on the rear chute flapper.
steps.expectedObservation: Cut filament end is flat and clean without a long stringy tail that jams the hall sensor.
steps.commonMistake: Allowing the external purge waste bin behind the printer to pile up to chute height, backing molten purges into the nozzle.

guides.verificationProcedure: Trigger an automated Load -> Unload cycle on the affected bay from the printer menu and confirm smooth feed and full retraction.

ifNotFixedBranches.label: Filament reaches hotend but clicks and refuses to extrude

guides.title: MSLA Resin Vat Clean, Build Plate Adhesion & Exposure Recovery
toolsNeeded: Nitrile gloves (minimum 6 mil)
UV400 safety glasses
Old resin support raft (for safe Vat Clean peel)
Silicone squeegee (NEVER metal scraper on film)
Paint strainer mesh funnel (190 micron)
partsNeeded: Replacement PFA/nFEP or ACF release film (if film has deep dents, clouding, or pinholes)
safetyWarnings: CHEMICAL & UV HAZARD: Uncured liquid photopolymer resin is a sensitizer and toxic to aquatic life. Always wear nitrile gloves (latex is permeable to resin monomers) and safety glasses.
NEVER home the Z-axis after a failed resin print without clearing cured debris from the vat first—driving cured plastic into the monochrome LCD shatters the glass immediately.
Never pour resin-contaminated IPA down household drains; cure waste in sunlight and dispose per local hazardous waste rules.
guides.serviceBoundaryNote: User-serviceable MSLA recovery. Internal UV COB LED driver replacement or mainboard repairs should be referred to manufacturer support.

modelSpecificMenuNotes.mdl_elegoo_saturn_4_ultra: Touchscreen -> Tools -> Tank Clean (15s). Place an old support raft press-held gently in one corner of the vat before running Tank Clean so the entire cured sheet peels up in one clean piece.
modelSpecificMenuNotes.mdl_anycubic_photon_mono_m7: Touchscreen -> Tools -> Vat Cleaning, then run R_E_R_F multiple-exposure test matrix whenever opening a new bottle/brand of resin.
modelSpecificMenuNotes.mdl_uniformation_gktwo: Enable Chamber Heater to 25–30°C and allow 20 minutes pre-heat before pressing Print.
modelSpecificMenuNotes.mdl_formlabs_form_4: Use the Form 4 Tank Inspection tool included in the Finish Kit to gently lift cured rafts; never run generic scraper blades across the LFD flexible film.

steps.title: Run Safe Full-Sheet Vat Clean & Filter Resin
steps.instruction: Put on nitrile gloves and safety glasses. Place an old cured support piece gently against one corner of the vat floor, run the printer’s 15-second "Tank Clean / Exposure Clean" function, and slowly peel up the corner raft—lifting all stuck cured islands off the PFA/FEP film at once without scraping. If debris tumbled loose, pour resin through a 190-micron paint filter back into the bottle and inspect the film over a dry paper towel for leaks.
steps.expectedObservation: Release film is completely clear of cured islands, pinholes, or sharp creases.
steps.commonMistake: Digging at stuck rafts with a hard plastic or metal spatula, puncturing the PFA film and leaking liquid resin onto the LCD screen.

steps.title: Stabilize Resin Temperature (25–30°C) & Mix Pigment
steps.instruction: Gently swirl or silicone-stir resin so settled titanium dioxide/grey pigments remix without whipping air bubbles. Warm the bottle in a warm water bath or run the printer’s chamber/vat heater to 25–30°C before starting.
steps.expectedObservation: Uniform resin color and fluid honey-free consistency with bubbles dissipated.
steps.commonMistake: Starting prints in an 16°C garage—cold viscosity prevents the build plate from squeezing down to 0.05 mm layer height, causing thick rafts or immediate plate detachment.

steps.title: Check Build Plate Leveling Mechanism & Orientation Suction
steps.instruction: Degrease the aluminum build plate with 99% IPA and dry completely. If your printer uses 4 manual leveling screws (e.g., GKtwo), re-level gently in an X-pattern; if your printer uses spring-sensor auto-leveling (e.g., Saturn 4 Ultra / Mars 5 Ultra / Form 4), verify the top clamp knob/lever is locked tight and inspect your slicer file to angle flat faces 30–45° and place ≥2.5 mm drain holes at the lowest cavity edge.
steps.expectedObservation: Zero unvented suction cups in slicer layer preview; build plate clean and dry.
steps.commonMistake: Hollowing a miniature torso to save resin without adding a vent hole near the build-plate side, creating a powerful plunger suction cup.

steps.title: Calibrate Bottom & Normal Exposure + Rest Time
steps.instruction: Add 1.0–1.5s "Rest Time After Retract / Wait Before Print" on bottom layers so viscous resin stops moving before UV fires. Run an exposure validation matrix (e.g., Cones of Calibration / Boxes of Calibration / R_E_R_F) to dial in tensile support strength.
steps.expectedObservation: Bottom raft adheres reliably yet releases cleanly with a bevelled scraper; tensile calibration pins connect cleanly.
steps.commonMistake: Cranking bottom exposure to 60+ seconds on a modern mono LCD, baking the raft onto the plate and shortening LCD lifespan.

guides.verificationProcedure: Print a 15-minute dimensional & tensile resin exposure calibration matrix before re-running large multi-hour plates.

ifNotFixedBranches.label: Print sticks now, but has vertical holes or solid cured blocks

materials.name: PLA / PLA+ (Polylactic Acid)
materials.enclosureRequirement: Not required (open air preferred for overhangs)
materials.dryingGuidance: 45–50°C for 4–6 hours if brittle or stringing. Store <25% RH.
materials.coolingGuidance: 100% part cooling fan after layer 1–2; vent enclosed printers so chamber stays <38°C to prevent extruder heat creep.
materials.hardwareCompatibilityNotes: Supported by virtually all FDM printers. High-speed profiles (300+ mm/s) typically run 215–225°C; matte/silk PLA has lower layer adhesion than standard PLA.
materials.safetyGuidance: Low odor (lactide); normal room ventilation recommended. Low heat deflection (~55°C)—parts deform in hot cars.

materials.name: PETG (Glycol-Modified PET)
materials.enclosureRequirement: Not required (open air preferred for overhangs)
materials.dryingGuidance: 60–65°C for 6–8 hours. Highly hygroscopic—even factory-sealed spools often string until dried.
materials.coolingGuidance: 20–50% part cooling (up to 70% on overhangs/high-speed machines); 0% for first 3 layers.
materials.hardwareCompatibilityNotes: Avoid sustained >245°C on older PTFE-lined MK8 hotends (e.g., stock Ender-3 V2); all-metal hotends preferred. Use Textured/Satin PEI, or apply PVA glue release barrier on Smooth PEI or bare glass.
materials.safetyGuidance: Low VOC emission; ventilate workspace normally.

materials.name: ABS (Acrylonitrile Butadiene Styrene)
materials.coolingGuidance: 0–30% part cooling inside warm chamber (45–60°C chamber prevents layer splitting and corner warping).
materials.hardwareCompatibilityNotes: Requires all-metal hotend, heated bed capable of ≥95°C (excludes Bambu A1 mini 80°C bed), and full draft-free enclosure.
materials.safetyGuidance: Emits styrene VOCs and ultrafine particles during printing. Use an enclosed HEPA + activated carbon scrubber or exhaust ducting outside.

materials.name: ASA (Acrylonitrile Styrene Acrylate)
materials.coolingGuidance: 0–25% fan in warm enclosed chamber; pre-heat soak bed at 105°C for 15 minutes before starting print.
materials.hardwareCompatibilityNotes: Requires enclosed printer with ≥100°C bed and all-metal hotend.
materials.safetyGuidance: Emits styrene/acrylate fumes—requires enclosure filtration or active exhaust ventilation.

materials.name: TPU 95A / 85A (Thermoplastic Polyurethane)
materials.enclosureRequirement: Not required (open air preferred for overhangs)
materials.dryingGuidance: 55–65°C for 6–8 hours. Extremely moisture-sensitive—wet TPU foams and strings heavily.
materials.hardwareCompatibilityNotes: Direct-drive extruders strongly recommended. Do NOT feed soft 95A/85A TPU through multi-material hubs (Bambu AMS, Creality CFS, Anycubic ACE, Prusa MMU) unless using certified high-hardness AMS-compatible TPU; load from external low-friction spool holder.
materials.safetyGuidance: Bonds aggressively to Smooth PEI—use Textured PEI or apply PVA glue stick as a release agent!

materials.name: PA6 / PA12 Nylon
materials.dryingGuidance: 75–85°C for 10–12 hours, AND print directly out of an active heated drybox (<15% RH)—PA6 absorbs room moisture within 2 hours.
materials.coolingGuidance: 0–15% part cooling to maximize inter-layer crystalline strength.
materials.hardwareCompatibilityNotes: Requires ≥280°C all-metal hotend and enclosed chamber; specialized PA glue or Garolite/G10 plate often required for warp resistance.
materials.safetyGuidance: Caprolactam emissions—print in enclosed ventilated space.

materials.name: PC (Polycarbonate)
materials.coolingGuidance: 0–15% fan; active heated chamber (55–65°C on QIDI Plus4 / Prusa CORE One / Creality K2 Plus / Bambu H2D) greatly reduces warping.
materials.hardwareCompatibilityNotes: Requires ≥290°C all-metal hotend and ≥110°C bed. Always use release glue on PEI so cooling shrinkage does not delaminate PEI film.
materials.safetyGuidance: High hotend & bed temperatures; ventilate BPA/trace VOC fumes.

materials.name: PVA & BVOH (Water-Soluble Support)
materials.enclosureRequirement: Not required (open air preferred for overhangs)
materials.dryingGuidance: 45–50°C for 6–8 hours; MUST stay sealed in a drybox (<15% RH) during the entire print.
materials.coolingGuidance: 50–100% fan; never leave PVA idling hot at >205°C for long periods or it caramelizes into an insoluble black tar clog!
materials.hardwareCompatibilityNotes: Best suited to true dual-nozzle/IDEX/toolchanger printers (UltiMaker S5 BB core, Prusa XL, Snapmaker Artisan, Bambu H2D) rather than single-nozzle multiplexers where PVA contaminates structural layers.
materials.safetyGuidance: Dissolve in warm tap water per manufacturer disposal limits.

materials.name: Carbon-Fiber & Glass-Fiber Filled (PLA-CF, PETG-CF, PA-CF, PPA-CF)
materials.dryingGuidance: Dry per base polymer (65°C PETG-CF; 80°C PA-CF/PPA-CF for 10h).
materials.hardwareCompatibilityNotes: MANDATORY HARDENED HARDWARE: Chopped carbon/glass fibers ream out brass or stainless nozzles within 250g and wear unhardened extruder gears. A 0.4 mm hardened steel / SiC / tungsten-carbide nozzle is minimum; 0.6 mm nozzle strongly recommended to prevent fiber bridging clogs.
materials.safetyGuidance: Avoid sanding dry CF/GF dust without a P100/FFP3 respirator; wash hands after handling raw prints with exposed micro-fibers.

materials.name: Standard & ABS-Like 405nm Photopolymer Resin
materials.dryingGuidance: Keep bottle capped away from daylight/window UV; maintain liquid temperature at 25–30°C during printing.
materials.coolingGuidance: N/A (Post-wash in ≥95% IPA for 3–5 min, air dry completely until matte, then 405nm UV post-cure 2–5 min).
materials.hardwareCompatibilityNotes: Compatible with all 405nm monochrome LCD & LFD printers (Formlabs requires Open Material Mode or matching Formlabs cartridge).
materials.exposureNotesResin: Typical 0.05 mm starting baseline on modern Mono LCDs: 25–32s Bottom Exposure (4–6 bottom layers), 1.8–2.8s Normal Exposure, 1.0s Wait-Before-Print rest time. Always verify with an exposure test matrix per bottle pigment.
materials.safetyGuidance: Wear nitrile gloves and safety glasses; ventilate workspace; cure all wash sludge and paper towels in UV before disposal.

materials.name: Tough, Engineering & High-Viscosity Resins
materials.dryingGuidance: Pre-warm resin to 28–35°C! High-viscosity urethane/engineering resins fail to squeeze thin in cold rooms.
materials.coolingGuidance: Two-stage clean IPA wash + heated UV post-cure (often 60°C thermal + 405nm UV cure required to reach rated mechanical strength).
materials.hardwareCompatibilityNotes: Heated-vat printers (Uniformation GKtwo, Phrozen Mighty Revo, Formlabs Form 4, Saturn 4 Ultra 16K) strongly preferred. Increase Wait-Before-Print (Rest Time After Retract) to 2.0–3.0s.
materials.exposureNotesResin: Typical 0.05 mm Mono LCD baseline: 30–40s Bottom Exposure, 2.8–4.5s Normal Exposure, slower peel/lift speed (40–60 mm/min) on non-tilting vats.
materials.safetyGuidance: Strict nitrile PPE, eye splash protection, and organic vapor filtration.

errorCodes.verifiedMeaning: Heatbed temperature / thermistor anomaly or AI print-monitoring detection alert (e.g., spaghetti / nozzle clump / purge chute pile-up).
likelyCauses: Heatbed NTC thermistor wire open/short circuit or loose connector under bed.
AI camera detected detached spaghetti strands or excess purge buildup in rear chute (0300-1200 / 0300-8000 subcodes).
recommendedChecks: Scan the exact 16-digit HMS QR code on the touchscreen to isolate thermal vs AI monitoring subcode.
For thermal subcodes, inspect heatbed cable strain relief (especially early A1 units) and do not operate if cable jacket is bulged or damaged.
For chute/spaghetti subcodes, clear rear purge chute flapper and inspect chamber camera lens cleanliness.

errorCodes.verifiedMeaning: Toolhead / Extruder motor overload, step loss, or toolhead communication anomaly.
likelyCauses: Clogged nozzle or heat-creep softened PLA jammed inside extruder gears.
Loose USB-C / TH board toolhead cable connector.
recommendedChecks: Unload filament; if stuck, heat nozzle to 250°C and perform cold-pull / extruder gear inspection.
Power off and reseat the toolhead TH board cable connector.

errorCodes.verifiedMeaning: AMS assist motor overload — failed to feed or failed to pull back filament from toolhead.
likelyCauses: Tangled spool, dented cardboard spool rim slipping on AMS rollers, or brittle PLA broken inside internal AMS PTFE hub.
Tight PTFE tube bend right above the toolhead rubbing against the top glass lid.
recommendedChecks: Disconnect PTFE coupler above toolhead and check whether filament pulls back smoothly by hand.
Inspect AMS internal 4-to-1 hub for broken filament fragments and check toolhead filament cutter lever.

errorCodes.verifiedMeaning: Stuck filament detected via Nextruder Loadcell pressure spike.
likelyCauses: Partial nozzle clog or heat creep creating high back-pressure measured by the Nextruder heatsink loadcell.
Tangled spool on holder or excessive PTFE reverse-Bowden drag.
recommendedChecks: Verify spool rotates freely without crossed windings.
Open Nextruder idler swivel arm, brush debris from planetary drive gear, and run Control -> Cold Pull.

errorCodes.verifiedMeaning: Loadcell sensor reading out of range, tare failure, or mechanical preload interference during probing.
likelyCauses: Overtightened Nextruder heatsink mounting screws placing static stress on the loadcell beam.
Printer workbench vibrating during loadcell tare, or damaged loveboard loadcell plug.
recommendedChecks: Inspect LoveBoard loadcell 4-pin connector seating inside the Nextruder cover.
Ensure hotend nozzle is clean and run Control -> Calibration & Tests -> Loadcell Test on a rigid surface.

errorCodes.verifiedMeaning: Strain gauge leveling sensor data transmission anomaly or poor contact.
likelyCauses: Loose 4-pin wiring connector on the under-bed strain gauge leveling MCU board.
Purged plastic debris wedged between the Z-platform frame and heated bed blocking sensor deflection.
recommendedChecks: Inspect beneath the heated bed platform and clear any fallen filament scraps.
Power off printer, unplug and firmly reseat the strain-gauge sensor harness connectors under the bed, then run Self-Check.

errorCodes.verifiedMeaning: Extruder nozzle is not heating as expected (Thermal Runaway / Heater Verification Protection).
likelyCauses: Loose ceramic heater ring or thermistor plug on the printhead breakout PCB.
Missing silicone hotend sock allowing high-speed part cooling fan to chill the ceramic heater.
recommendedChecks: Power off and cool completely. Confirm the silicone sock is installed squarely over the Unicorn/K1 ceramic heater.
Remove toolhead cover and firmly reseat the white 2-pin heater and thermistor plugs on the toolhead PCB.

errorCodes.verifiedMeaning: Active Leveling correction out of range or capacitive leveling sensor noise.
likelyCauses: Plastic buildup on Print Core tip pushing glass plate down.
Torn silicone printhead nozzle seal or glass build plate thumbscrews skewed beyond 3 mm active range.
recommendedChecks: Clean both Print Core tips and inspect the rectangular silicone nozzle cover underneath the printhead.
Run Preferences -> Maintenance -> Build Plate -> Manual Leveling once to bring thumbscrews back within capacitive sensor range.

maintenance.title: Degrease Flexible PEI / Glass Build Surface
maintenance.intervalGuidance: Every 5–10 prints, or immediately after touching the print zone with bare hands
maintenance.procedureSummary: Wash cooled removable spring steel PEI plate at the sink with warm water and plain unscented dish soap; dry with clean paper towels.
maintenance.lubricantOrCleaner: Plain degreasing dish soap + warm water (99% IPA between washes for dust)
doNotApplyTo: Never apply Acetone to Textured Powder-Coated PEI, Cool Plates, or PC sheets
maintenance.safetyWarning: Allow heated bed to cool below 40°C before removing plate.

maintenance.title: Clean Carbon-Fiber X-Axis Rods (Dry Self-Lubricating)
applicableSystems: Bambu Lab X1 Carbon / P1S / P1P Carbon X-Gantry
maintenance.intervalGuidance: Every 300 print hours (monthly in heavy ABS/ASA use)
maintenance.procedureSummary: Spray 99% Isopropyl Alcohol onto a clean lint-free microfiber cloth and wipe carbon rods repeatedly while sliding toolhead gently until black graphite/VOC residue clears.
doNotApplyTo: NEVER apply grease, PTFE oil, or WD-40 to hollow carbon-fiber rods—lubricant traps dust into an abrasive paste that destroys the self-lubricating graphite bushings!
maintenance.safetyWarning: Power off printer and keep IPA spray away from camera/LiDAR lenses.

maintenance.title: Clean & Re-Lubricate Steel Linear Rails, Rods & Z Lead Screws
maintenance.intervalGuidance: Every 250–500 print hours (or when firmware prompts linear rail lubrication)
maintenance.procedureSummary: Wipe old darkened grease and filament dust off Z-axis trapezoid lead screws and steel linear rails first, then apply a thin film of synthetic PTFE/lithium grease to lead screws and light machine/super-lube oil to steel linear rail carriages.
maintenance.lubricantOrCleaner: Synthetic PTFE Grease (Z lead screws) & Light Synthetic Machine Oil (MGN steel linear rails)
doNotApplyTo: Timing belts (rubber/PU belts must stay dry)
maintenance.safetyWarning: Power off steppers; keep fingers clear of Z lead screw couplers and pinch zones.

maintenance.title: Brush Extruder Drive Gears & Clear Heatsink Fan Fins
maintenance.intervalGuidance: Every 250 print hours (every 100 hours when printing abrasive CF/GF or dusty matte PLA)
maintenance.procedureSummary: Open extruder idler access door or cover, brush packed plastic shavings out of drive gear teeth with a stiff nylon/brass brush, and blow dust out of the hotend heatsink fan blades while holding the fan hub stationary.
maintenance.lubricantOrCleaner: Dry nylon brush & compressed air (hold fan blades still!)
doNotApplyTo: Never spin cooling fans to high RPM with compressed air—back-EMF voltage spikes can fry fan MOSFETs on the toolhead PCB!
maintenance.safetyWarning: Power off and cool hotend below 35°C before removing toolhead shrouds.

maintenance.title: Inspect PFA / nFEP / ACF Release Film & Screen Protector
maintenance.intervalGuidance: Inspect after any failed print; replace film typically every 30,000–60,000 peel layers (or immediately if deep dents/pinholes appear)
maintenance.procedureSummary: Drain and filter resin through a 190-micron strainer, rinse vat with IPA using ultra-soft microfiber/PEC-PADs (paper towels scratch FEP!), place clean vat on dry white paper towel filled with water/IPA for 10 min to verify zero pinhole leaks, and check glass screen protector edges.
doNotApplyTo: Coarse paper towels on FEP/PFA film (causes clouding)
maintenance.safetyWarning: Always wear nitrile gloves and eye protection when draining or cleaning resin vats.

maintenance.title: Clean & Lubricate Resin Z-Axis Ball Screw / Dual Linear Rails
maintenance.intervalGuidance: Every 3–6 months or if Z-axis squeaks during lift
maintenance.procedureSummary: Cover the resin vat/LCD completely so grease cannot contaminate optics, wipe old hardened grease off the Z lead screw/ball screw, and apply white lithium or synthetic PTFE grease.
maintenance.lubricantOrCleaner: White Lithium or Synthetic PTFE Grease
doNotApplyTo: LCD screen glass, Fresnel optics, or tilting vat hinge sensors
maintenance.safetyWarning: Protect the monochrome LCD with its vat cover before lubricating above it.
